jobs.title: Trading & Execution
jobs.descriptionHtml:
Trading & Execution

We are a private family office seeking an experienced Execution Trader to join our investment team. As a small, collaborative firm, every member of our team plays a meaningful role in the investment process. This position offers direct exposure to the firm’s Principal and the opportunity to make an immediate impact on portfolio implementation and trading operations.

We are looking for an experienced institutional execution trader who enjoys working in a lean, entrepreneurial environment where responsibility is earned and contributions are highly visible.

Responsibilities

Execute trades across equities, options, ETFs, futures, and other listed securities. Manage the full lifecycle of orders with a focus on execution quality, liquidity, timing, and market impact. Monitor markets throughout the trading day and communicate relevant developments to the investment team.Coordinate with brokers, counterparties, and trading venues.Perform post-trade analysis and continually evaluate execution performance.Assist with trade allocations, reconciliations, and operational workflows.Help improve trading processes, technology, and execution infrastructure.Work closely with the investment team on portfolio implementation and risk management.

Qualifications:

5+ years of institutional execution trading experience. Experience at a leading investment bank, hedge fund, asset manager, proprietary trading firm, or family office. Strong understanding of equity market structure, and electronic trading platforms. Experience executing institutional-sized orders. Familiarity with options and futures markets is preferred. Excellent organizational skills, attention to detail, and communication. Ability to remain composed and make sound decisions in fast-moving markets. High integrity and discretion.

What We’re Looking For:

The ideal candidate is someone who:

Is a team player who enjoys working in a close-knit environment.Takes ownership and thrives without unnecessary bureaucracy. Has excellent judgment and attention to detail. Is calm under pressure and disciplined in execution. Constantly looks for ways to improve processes and efficiency. Wants to be part of a small team where their work has a direct impact on investment performance.

What We Offer:

A collaborative, tight-knit team with direct access to decision-makers. A high level of responsibility and autonomy. Exposure to all aspects of the investment process. Competitive compensation with performance-based incentives. An opportunity to help build and improve the firm’s trading capabilities over the long term.

jobs.title: Head of Research
jobs.descriptionHtml:
Head of Research

About Deeter Analytics

Deeter Analytics is a privately held investment research and trading firm managing its own capital across public markets, alternatives, and private investments.

We operate with a small, senior, high-performance team within a deeply entrepreneurial culture. We value autonomy, judgment, clarity, and technical rigor. We hire very few people, expect a great deal from them, and invest heavily in long-term performance and trust.

This environment suits sharp, self-directed thinkers who can hold ambiguity, exercise independent judgment, and translate complex inputs into clear action.


Role Overview

The Mandate:

The Principal operates in fast-moving, highly competitive global markets where asymmetric information and early insight define success. We require a research leader who functions as a force multiplier—someone who transforms complexity into clarity and conviction into profitable action.

You are the engine that converts raw information into durable advantage.

We are looking for a strategic thinker and relentless operator who sees what others miss and moves before consensus forms.

The Requirement: Intellectual and Strategic Mastery

You are capable of navigating any information environment—public markets, private capital, geopolitics, technology, macro, and industry-specific ecosystems—and extracting actionable truth in real time.

  • Signal Extraction: You distinguish material insight from background noise. You build systems and teams that surface what matters and discard what doesn’t.

  • Trend Origination: You identify emerging structural shifts before they are obvious and design frameworks for early positioning.

  • Narrative Intelligence: You continuously map prevailing and emerging market narratives across sectors and asset classes, understanding what ideas are gaining traction, where, and why—without defaulting to consensus.

  • Analytical Rigor: You do not accept surface narratives. You deconstruct incentives, second-order effects, and hidden dependencies.

  • Synthesis: You integrate disparate data points into coherent, tradeable worldviews.

  • Communication Precision: You translate complex analysis into clear, decisive guidance for traders and investment teams.

Core Attributes

  • Raw Agency and Intelligence : You are proactive, reason independently, challenge assumptions, and build original theses from first principles.

  • Judgment Under Uncertainty: You make high-quality decisions with incomplete information.

  • Ownership Mentality: You treat outcomes as personal responsibilities, not abstractions. You take action on your own without being told what to do.

  • Integrity of Thought: You resist groupthink and protect intellectual honesty.

The Scope

Your immediate priority is to build and lead a world-class research operation that consistently generates early, differentiated insight.

You will:

  • Architect and oversee a high-performance team of analysts and news monitors.

  • Design information pipelines that deliver real-time, high-signal intelligence.

  • Identify and validate emerging opportunities across public and private markets.

  • Partner closely with the Principal to develop a forward-looking worldview.

  • Translate macro, sectoral, and thematic views into actionable investment strategies.

  • Continuously refine frameworks for opportunity identification and risk assessment.

You will function as the Principal’s closest intellectual partner in shaping how the firm understands and engages with the world.

The Incentive

We believe in alignment.

Your compensation will reflect the quality, durability, and impact of your insights. Exceptional performance and sustained edge will be rewarded through meaningful participation in the upside.

To Apply

Send a brief note describing a time you identified a critical opportunity or risk before others did—and how you turned that insight into tangible results.

jobs.title: Junior Quantitative Researcher
jobs.descriptionHtml:
Junior Quantitative Researcher

About the role

Deeter Analytics is a privately held investment research and trading firm managing its own capital across public markets. After years of discretionary success, we think we have some unique ways of seeing the market, and we pair sharp human judgment with modern AI to act on them.

A lot of what we trade starts as a hunch at the desk: a pattern that keeps showing up, a relationship that feels like it should hold, a setup someone wants to trust but doesn't yet. We're hiring a Junior Quantitative Researcher to turn those hunches into evidence, and evidence into signals the desk actually uses. You'll take questions from the traders, test them honestly against the data, and come back in plain language: what holds, what doesn't, how strong, since when, and where it breaks. This is not a systematic seat: your models won't trade on their own, and you won't be one factor in an anonymous alpha pool. Your work is done when a trader understands it, trusts it, and acts on it. It's an entry point into a serious seat: as your signals prove out, they get more weight in the book, and you get more scope. The role is full-time and fully remote, US-based, overlapping the desk on US market hours.

What you'll own

• The question queue. Desk hunches in, answers out. You scope the question, run the study, and come back sometimes same-day with what the data says, at the depth the question deserves.

• The signal shelf. A growing library of signals and screens the desk trades around (earnings and event setups, positioning and flow extremes, regime and factor context) each with a documented edge, known failure modes, and live tracking against expectation. You retire what decays.

• The evidence standard. Event studies, conditioning analyses, base rates, and walk-forward checks that hold up: point-in-time data, no leakage, no survivorship, costs counted, multiple-testing restraint. A backtest here is a way to kill an idea, not to sell it.

• The quant read. The recurring numbers layer under the desk's picture of the market (regime, factor moves, breadth, positioning) feeding the morning picture rather than duplicating it.

• The research data. Clean, point-in-time datasets (prices, fundamentals, earnings calendars, options and positioning) organized so every number you've ever reported traces back to code and data.

• AI leverage. Use modern AI tools to test more ideas, read more literature, and write cleaner code than one person otherwise could, and verify what they give you.

Who you are

We hire for demonstrated judgment and how you think, not for pedigree. This is a junior seat, so we don't expect a markets résumé — the best evidence usually comes from wherever you've already done rigorous quantitative work. We look for signs that you are:

• Rigorous where it counts. You think in base rates, sample sizes, and conditioning; you know what autocorrelation, overlapping windows, and fat tails do to naive statistics, and you'd rather report a small honest edge than a large fragile one.

• Hypothesis-driven. You start from a mechanism (why would this work, who's on the other side, why hasn't it been arbitraged away) and let the data disappoint you, not the other way around.

• A translator. Your finished product is a chart and a paragraph a non-quant acts on. If the desk can't understand it, it isn't done.

• Comfortable finding nothing. "There's nothing there" is a result you deliver without flinching: a clean negative saves the desk real money, and you never dress noise up as signal to give someone the answer they wanted.

• Genuinely curious about markets. You want to know why prices move. You don't need professional markets experience, you need to care about the answer.

• Low ego and coachable. You take feedback well, update quickly when the facts change, and care more about the answer than the credit.

How you work

• At desk speed, without cutting corners. A rough answer today often beats a perfect answer next week; a deep study is worth a month when the stakes justify it. You know which question is which, and you label your answers accordingly.

• Kill your own results first. Before anyone else sees a number, you've gone hunting for the leak, the regime dependence, and the artifact that would explain it away.

• Reproducible by default. Versioned data and code; any signal or study can be re-run months later and give the same answer.

• Signal over noise. You surface the few things that matter, track what you've shipped, and say so plainly when something stops working.

• AI-native. Fluent with modern AI tools for research, coding, and literature triage, and disciplined about checking their output.

• Self-directed. You thrive working remotely with low guardrails, managing your own time and flagging what needs attention without being asked.

Core skills

• Statistics and probability. Regression and its failure modes, hypothesis testing, bootstrap and resampling, thinking clearly about uncertainty in small and messy samples.

• Python data stack. pandas, NumPy, SQL, and plotting that makes a point; notebooks that read top to bottom, graduating to scripts when a study becomes a signal.

• Backtest and event-study hygiene. Point-in-time discipline, survivorship and look-ahead awareness, transaction-cost sanity, walk-forward validation, restraint about how many things you tested.

• Market data. Comfort with prices, returns, fundamentals, and earnings calendars; options or positioning data a plus.

• ML as a tool, not an identity. Regularized regression and gradient boosting when they beat something simpler, interpretability first. This is a statistics-first seat, not a deep-learning one.

• Crisp communication. Compressing a study into exactly what a trader needs to know, now.

What we offer

• A seat inside a live trading operation, with a direct line to the traders who act on your evidence.

• Fast feedback: when a signal proves out, you watch it get used — and you'll know precisely what your work changed.

• A well-capitalized firm with a distinctive approach to markets.

• A deliberate growth path: own the question queue first, then take on a bigger slice of the research agenda as you prove out.

• A small, low-ego, fully remote team.

• Compensation: $120k - $170k + bonus.

jobs.title: Head of Risk
jobs.descriptionHtml:
About the role

Deeter Analytics is a privately held investment research and trading firm managing its own capital across global public markets. We pair sharp human judgment with modern AI to act on a distinctive way of seeing markets, and we run a concentrated, thesis-driven book that moves as the world does.

We’re hiring a Head of Risk to own everything that happens after a position goes on. You’ll know positions and the reasoning behind them, read the book daily against the firm’s current views, and say plainly when something no longer belongs: a view that has run its course, two positions that contradict each other, an exposure that accumulated without anyone deciding to have it. You’ll own the firm’s picture of its own exposures and define what we need to see to manage them. You report directly to the principal.

 

This is an individual contributor seat, built from scratch: no team to manage, no outside investors to report to, and no inherited framework. The work is yours to do, not to delegate.

 

What you’ll own

  • The map of the book. A living inventory of every position: why it’s on, what would take it off, and what it’s exposed to, by name, theme and factor.

  • Thesis hygiene. A daily read of positions against the firm’s current views, with stale, contradictory or mis-sized positions flagged the day they happen.

  • The clean-up. Positions nobody is watching, residual pieces of old trades, exposures that drifted. You find them and get them resolved.

  • Exposure and scenario views sized to how we actually trade, in terms the principal will act on.

  • Counterparty, financing and operational exposures across our brokers and platforms: known, sized, and on the same map as the positions.

  • What we need to see. You define the data and views this seat requires and the tech team builds to your spec.

  • The daily note. One short, decision-ready view each day: what changed, what’s stale, what needs a decision.

 

What this is not

Not a PM or trader seat, and not a path to one. Not a quant seat. Not the desk’s housekeeping; execution and position maintenance stay with the trading desk. You won’t run a view of your own or be asked where markets are going; you’ll be asked whether the book is consistent with the principal’s view and the evidence behind it. You don’t set limits and there is no risk committee; the principal decides. What you have is a direct line.

 

Who you are

We hire for demonstrated judgment and how you think, not for pedigree. You’ve done this job (at a fund, a family office, a prop desk, or on the risk side of a bank) and you know what a clean risk process looks like because you’ve run one. We look for evidence that you are:

  • Careful by temperament. Loose ends bother you.

  • Fluent in risk, allergic to taking it. You understand positioning, derivatives, factor exposure, liquidity and counterparty risk well enough to see what a discretionary book is really exposed to, and you have no wish to express a view of your own.

  • Comfortable with a principal who changes direction fast. You don’t need the world to be orderly; you make the book orderly inside a fast-moving process.

  • A plain communicator. You say “this doesn’t belong anymore” in one sentence and back it with the numbers in the next.

  • Low ego, truth-seeking, and driven. Quick to update when the facts change, and unbothered by telling an experienced principal that a position is stale.

 

How you work

  • Self-directed. Nobody will hand you a limits framework or a risk committee. You’ll define the process.

  • Hands on. You do the work yourself, every day.

  • Builder minded. You can specify, and ideally prototype, what you need to see (Python, SQL or spreadsheets) rather than waiting for a system.

  • Proportionate. You know which exposures matter for a book like ours and which are institutional theatre, and you spend your attention accordingly.

  • AI-native. Fluent with modern AI tools for surveillance, synthesis and reporting, with a trust-but-verify discipline on their output.

  • Fast and collaborative. You operate at the speed of markets, work closely with the trading desk and the tech team, and make the people around you sharper.

 

Core skills

  • Book reading. Seeing a concentrated book as a set of exposures rather than a list of tickers.

  • Thesis-to-position mapping. Translating a discretionary view into what should and shouldn’t be on, and keeping that mapping current.

  • Scenario thinking. Factor, theme and liquidity scenarios that produce decisions, not reports.

  • Counterparty and operational awareness. Knowing where a book is exposed beyond the positions themselves, and keeping that in view.

  • Data specification. Knowing what a risk function needs from position, broker and internal data, and asking for it precisely.

  • Operating discipline. Daily rhythm, documentation that survives you, and follow-through on every flag until it’s resolved.

 

What we offer

  • A direct line to the principal and a seat beside the decisions your work protects.

  • A well-capitalized firm with a distinctive approach to markets and a clean slate to define how risk works here.

  • A small, discreet team that values intellectual honesty, independent judgment and speed over hierarchy and process.

  • Upside tied to how much cleaner and better-protected the book is because you exist.

  • Remote; US market hours.
